chapter: Three Deuces and 52nd Street with Tatum
title: Getting along with Tatum; oversleeping at the Howard; Les Paul and Buddy Rich
summary: Tatum called him Grimey Joe and he called Tatum uncle; he was late once in Washington, and Les Paul and Buddy Rich came to hear them.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: So, you got along well with Tatum?

Oh good, we had no problems. I used to call him uncle. He used to call me Grimey Joe, Grimey Joe. All the time Grimey or Grimey Joe I said, 'All right uncle'. You're my uncle.' He didn't like me say 'I ain't your uncle.' We had a good time. We had no problems. Never. The whole time I was with that group

I missed -- I was late once. I just overslept. I didn't have a clock. We were in Washington at the Howard Theater and boy when I woke up, I said "oh no" mmhm. I did it, finally did it, and when I got there, they was on the stage. Ain't nobody said a word though. They didn't chastise me, they didn't say a word. I wish they had something -- ha ha, they knew it wasn't no habit of mine, they knew that something was wrong. I just didn't get up. But that was the only time. I'd always be the first one downstairs practising, trying to get my part. Les Paul used to come & listen to us.
In California. Buddy Rich used to come and sit in with us, while he was in the Army. Right in The Streets of Paris.
